equivalents.note: The Tibetan has 'dod pa, 'desire', for āsā, 'hope', in a line that reads 'makes the desire-raining leaves and fruit fall' ('dod pa 'bab pa'i lo 'bras 'bab par byed), with 'bab pa where the Bengali has bahala, 'abundant'.
The line has mkhas pa, 'the learned', where the comment (cp.45.m4) has rig pa dang ldan pa'i skye bo, 'people endowed with knowledge'.
The Tibetan renders cheba bhebau as a pair of verbs, gcod dang gtub pa, 'cut and chop'.
The Tibetan has no vocative: where the Bengali addresses the fool (re mūṛha), rmongs nyid, 'the deluded one himself', becomes the subject who takes to existence (srid par mos).
The Tibetan has shing mchog, 'finest tree', as if reading taruvara, the form in which Munidatta cites the line (suna taruvara, cp.45.m6).
The Tibetan has no negative, 'cut that tree's branches from the very root' (shing de'i yal ga rtsa ba nyid nas gcod), where the Bengali has root, not branch (mūla na ḍāla).
The Tibetan renders utprekṣita with a verb of seeing, nye bar blta, 'regards [it] as', not with a term of poetics.
The Tibetan has 'the power of the guru's word' (bla ma'i gsung gi mthu) where the Sanskrit has 'the flow of the guru's word' (guruvacanapravāha), as if reading prabhāva.
The Tibetan renders the asampradāya yogins as 'yogins lacking instruction' (man ngag dang bral ba'i rnal 'byor pa), with man ngag, its usual word for upadeśa.
Here gurusampradāyāt becomes bla ma'i gsung gi drin las, 'through the grace of the guru's word'.
The Tibetan adds the guru's word: bla ma'i gsung gi lam gyi rjes su bsngags pa, 'praise of the path of the guru's word', for mārgānuśaṃsā.

questions: cutting (cp.45.3b): no equivalent. For chebai, 'cuts', the Tibetan line has dpyod pa, 'examines' ('the wise examine by the guru's measure'), an interpretation or perhaps a corruption of gcod pa; the other lines and the comment (cp.45.m4, gcod par byed) have gcod.

adhimukti (cp.45.m2): no equivalent. For pañcendriyeṇa śākhām adhimucya, 'resolving on the five senses as its branches', the Tibetan has dbang po lnga'i yal ga las grol ba, 'freed from the branches of the five senses', taking the root muc as 'release' rather than 'resolve' (mos).

ocean (cp.45.m5): no equivalent. For saṃsāraduḥkhavāridhau ṣaṭitvā patanti the Tibetan has 'khor ba'i sdug bsngal gyis 'khor zhing 'gro ba drug tu ltung bar 'gyur, 'circling in the suffering of saṃsāra they fall into the six realms', with no ocean; it seems to take Shastri's ṣaṭitvā as ṣaṭ, 'six'.
branch (cp.45.m6): the Tibetan comment has nothing for the citation ḍālam iti; the lines (1a, 5b) have yal ga.
